addedResources.name: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
addedResources.use: arXiv:2212.08073v1, Sections 3.1 and 4.1 and Appendix C.2: distinguish critique/revision data from constitution-conditioned comparison labels and trace the principle into label provenance. Read and audit the examples; no large-model RL reproduction is required.

units.title: Policy-dependent preference data and pairwise, listwise and tie labels
outcomes: Specify whose preferences a dataset represents, under which rubric and prompt distribution.
Trace each comparison to its generating policy, sampling settings and presentation order.
Convert rankings into strict pairs without silently turning ties, missing judgments or ratings into wins.
units.why: A preference label describes a comparison under a collection process, not an absolute quality certificate. That process defines what the later reward or policy fit can claim.

next.note: Check whether the collection process measures the intended preference.

study.title: The RLHF Book: Chapter 10, The Nature of Preferences; Chapter 11, Preference Data
study.locator: Chapter 11: Collecting Preference Data through Structured Preference Data, including Interfaces, Rankings vs. Ratings and Multiturn Data; Open Questions in RLHF Preference Data
study.depth: Skip Sourcing and Contracts. For the specification problem, also read Chapter 10, When Preference Replaces Correctness and Complexity of Optimizing Preferences, at https://rlhfbook.com/c/10-preferences.html. Do not repeat the basic judge survey from Model judges and human review.

study.title: CS336 Spring 2026 Assignment 5 supplement: inspect HH
study.locator: Section 6.2, Looking at Preference Data, Problem `look_at_hh`, parts (a) and (b), printed p. 16

focus: Record prompt source, generator checkpoint, decoding settings, rubric, labeler identity or type, displayed order and raw votes before making chosen/rejected records.

Preference collection often calls data from the same model family on-policy. This is not the strict RL definition of samples from the current update's policy. Off-policy pairs are usable, but coverage must be tested rather than assumed.
A ranking creates dependent pairs within a prompt. Preserve the ranking and prompt group so expanding it does not silently overweight prompts with more candidates.
Separate indifference, both-bad, uncertainty and missing labels. A rating difference is not automatically a calibrated preference probability.
units.reproduce: Without notes, draw the provenance chain from a sampled prompt to a training pair. For candidate IDs `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` with ranks `[1, 2, 2, 4]`, list the five strict winner-loser pairs and retain the tie separately. State which weighting rule would give this prompt the same total weight as a prompt with only one pair.
traps: Treating chosen as correct. Two wrong answers can still have a meaningful relative preference.
Splitting expanded pairs randomly. The same prompt, conversation or candidate can then cross the train/evaluation boundary.
Discarding the source collection after merging HH. Helpful, harmless and rejection-sampled data need separate audit slices.

selfTest.q: Does changing the generator leave the preference task unchanged?
selfTest.a: The rubric may stay fixed, but the compared response distribution changes. New failure modes and harder or easier comparisons can change observed agreement and learned behavior.

selfTest.q: How many strict pairs come from ranks `[1, 2, 2, 4]`?
selfTest.a: Five: `a` beats `b`, `c` and `d`; `b` and `c` each beat `d`. The `b`/`c` tie supplies no strict winner.

selfTest.q: Can an indifference label enter ordinary binary DPO unchanged?
selfTest.a: No. Declare a policy such as excluding it from the strict-pair objective while reporting it, or using an explicitly defined soft-label or tie-aware objective. Do not pick a winner arbitrarily.

practice.name: CS336 Assignment 5 supplement: `look_at_hh`
practice.locator: Section 6.2, parts (a) and (b): combine the four HH collections, retain source, remove multi-turn examples as specified, and inspect three helpful and three harmless comparisons
practice.note: This is a written/data-inspection problem, not an autograded one. Save accepted and excluded counts and your reasons for disagreeing with any labels. Use a bounded subset on CPU. The public handout and tests are study material; never publish assignment solutions.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Canonicalize Pairwise Preference Data
practice.note: Free. Public cases cover a three-candidate ranking, unsorted candidate input and two prompt records. Add your own tie and duplicate-ID rejection cases; the public cases do not establish those behaviors.

units.stopWhen: Your HH inspection retains source and exclusion counts, your strict-ranking converter passes the public examples, and your collection contract specifies ties, grouping and generator lineage.

fit.note: Chapters 10 and 11 cover the collection assumptions and label formats; the located HH problem and free ranking problem supply bounded practice.

units.title: Annotator agreement and noise, and position, length and style bias
outcomes: Measure agreement and presentation sensitivity while preserving raw votes, ties and abstentions.
Separate annotator error from rubric ambiguity, expertise gaps and legitimate preference differences.
Design a label-noise intervention and a length/style control before fitting the preference route.
units.why: An optimizer can learn an annotation interface's shortcuts as easily as its intended rubric. This audit extends Model judges and human review from evaluating outputs to checking the labels that will train a policy.

next.note: Fit a probability model only after defining what the votes mean.

study.title: InstructGPT: labeler selection and disagreement
study.locator: arXiv:2203.02155v1, Section 3.4, Human data collection; Appendix B.1, including the labeler selection procedure
study.depth: Read the collection and agreement protocol, not the large-model training recipe. The paper's agreement rates describe its recruited population, not a target for your audit.

study.title: The RLHF Book: collection bias and judge instructions
study.locator: Chapter 11, Bias: Things to Watch Out For in Data Collection and Open Questions in RLHF Preference Data; Chapter 5, Generative Reward Modeling, at https://rlhfbook.com/c/05-reward-models.html

study.title: A Long Way to Go: length as a confound
study.locator: arXiv:2310.03716v2, Sections 2 to 5: task setup, length-stratified reward analysis, length-only reward, interventions and preference analysis
study.depth: Read the controls and plots. Do not reproduce the paper's PPO training or use correlation alone as evidence of a causal length shortcut.

focus: Translate displayed-side labels back to response identity before comparing votes across order swaps. Report agreement, tie/abstention rates and counts by rubric axis and source.

Use blinded order swaps and identity removal; vary formatting or verbosity only after checking that the factual content and task constraints remain matched. Report both response lengths beside every win rate, using one fixed tokenizer and also a text-length measure.
Retain disagreements before adjudication. Record the reason and expertise needed; consensus can erase a real harmlessness/helpfulness trade-off rather than resolve it.
Flip labels only in a separate, versioned training intervention. Keep held-out labels untouched so robustness is not scored against the corruption you introduced.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, canonicalize two annotators' votes on four fixed pairs: `["a", "b", "tie", "a"]` and `["a", "a", "tie", "b"]`. Exact agreement, counting a shared tie as agreement, is 50%. Then derive that symmetric independent label flipping with probability 0.25 changes an underlying strict preference probability of 0.8 to 0.65. These are constructed checks, not estimates of human reliability.
traps: Calling delayed self-relabeling inter-annotator agreement. It measures your repeatability; use existing repeated labels or another consenting reviewer for between-person evidence.
Assuming a judge instruction to ignore length removes length bias. The instruction is a hypothesis to test, not a control that proves itself.
Treating all disagreement as random flips. Rubric conflict and population differences need separate slices, not just a noise rate.

selfTest.q: A judge chooses the left response in both orders. What does that establish?
selfTest.a: On that pair, its content preference is inconsistent under an order swap. More pairs are needed to estimate a position effect; a single pair does not identify a population bias.

selfTest.q: Why is 50% raw agreement not automatically chance agreement?
selfTest.a: Chance agreement depends on the label marginals and tie policy. Raw agreement alone does not adjust for skewed response preferences or annotator populations.

selfTest.q: Does a higher reward-length correlation prove the reward model ignores correctness?
selfTest.a: No. Correctness may require detail. Compare content-matched length interventions and inspect residual errors before attributing a shortcut.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: the raw-vote and adjudication ledger, order/identity/length/style audit, and a versioned annotator-noise intervention evaluated on untouched held-out labels.
units.stopWhen: Your audit distinguishes raw agreement from presentation sensitivity, includes untouched held-out labels, and reports paired lengths and sample counts beside every win rate.

fit.note: The collection protocol, book bias sections and length-intervention paper cover measurement design; the mini-project supplies the language-model label audit and noise comparison.

units.title: The Bradley-Terry likelihood and reward identifiability
outcomes: Derive a prompt-conditioned Bradley-Terry likelihood and its stable negative log-likelihood.
Identify the reward offsets that comparisons cannot recover, and distinguish them from score scale.
Check a repeated-vote fit and explain why ranking accuracy does not establish probability calibration.
units.why: DPO inherits its probability model from pairwise reward learning. Building on Maximum likelihood and MAP estimation and Logistic regression and stable binary cross-entropy, the new work is to state what a preference fit does not identify.

next.note: Carry the likelihood and its limits into a real reward head.

study.title: The RLHF Book: Chapter 5, Reward Modeling
study.locator: Training a Bradley-Terry Reward Model, from positive strengths through the log-sigmoid/softplus equivalence; Other Reward Model Variants, Balancing Multiple Comparisons Per Prompt and K-Wise Loss Function
study.depth: Derive the pairwise model fully. Read the grouped and listwise variants only to explain how expanding a ranking changes the sampling weights.

study.title: DPO: reward equivalence
study.locator: arXiv:2305.18290v3, Section 5.1, Your Language Model Is Secretly a Reward Model: Definition 1 and Lemmas 1 and 2; Appendix A.5, Proof of Lemma 1 and 2

focus: For fixed prompt \(x\), \(P(y_a \succ y_b \mid x)=\sigma(r(x,y_a)-r(x,y_b))\). Fit the sum or declared weighted mean of log likelihoods, not the log of an average probability.

Adding any prompt-only offset \(c(x)\) changes neither comparison probability nor the normalized KL-regularized optimal policy. Disconnected comparison components can have additional unidentified offsets without further assumptions.

With a fixed sigmoid link, multiplying all score differences changes probabilities, even when rankings stay fixed. If a separate temperature is also fitted, score scale and that temperature can be confounded.
A scalar reward is not a standalone correctness probability. Only the linked difference gives a pairwise probability under this model, and calibration must be assessed on held-out comparisons.
units.reproduce: For one prompt with two responses and ten recorded strict votes, eight favor the first and two the second. Derive the unregularized optimum score difference \(\log 4\), predicted probability 0.8 and mean negative log-likelihood 0.5004024235381879. On CPU with PyTorch 2.14.1 and `torch.float64`, evaluate stable binary cross-entropy on the ten labels and check the derivative at \(\log 4\) is zero within absolute tolerance \(10^{-12}\). Show that a shared offset leaves the likelihood unchanged but doubling the difference does not. This is an in-sample likelihood oracle, not a generalization score.
traps: Calling reward scale unidentifiable under a fixed logistic link. The free additive offset and the probability-sensitive multiplicative scale are different issues.
Reporting a finite unregularized optimum when all votes go one way. The logistic likelihood then favors an unbounded difference; an iteration limit can masquerade as a fitted scale.
Counting every expanded ranking pair as an independent annotation. Preserve prompt groups for weighting and uncertainty.

selfTest.q: Why can the two scores not be recovered separately from the ten votes?
selfTest.a: The likelihood depends only on their difference. An arbitrary common offset gives the same probabilities. Fix one score or impose a centering convention to choose a representative.

selfTest.q: What changes if both scores are multiplied by two?
selfTest.a: The ranking stays the same, but the difference doubles, so the sigmoid probability changes unless the difference is zero. This generally changes likelihood and calibration.

selfTest.q: Can equal rewards represent an explicit tie category in ordinary Bradley-Terry?
selfTest.a: No. They assign equal probabilities to the two strict outcomes. An explicit tie category requires an extension or a declared soft-label encoding; indifference and uncertainty remain different observations.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: the pairwise likelihood oracle, repeated-vote calibration check, and offset/scale and separated-vote regression tests for the reward route.
units.stopWhen: You derive and numerically check the repeated-vote optimum, distinguish offset from scale, and explain the all-one-label boundary without trusting a stopped solver.

fit.note: Chapter 5 supplies the likelihood and grouped/listwise context; the DPO equivalence proof supplies prompt-offset invariance, with executable likelihood practice in the mini-project.

units.title: Reward-model training contracts and reward shift across policies and lengths
outcomes: Train a bounded scalar reward head with a prompt-grouped split and an explicit padding/truncation contract.
Assess held-out ranking and pairwise probability calibration separately across generator and length slices.
Distinguish preference labels from outcome labels and diagnose a reward shortcut under distribution shift.
units.why: A correct loss can still train a scorer of padding, length or generator style. The research question is whether its rankings and probabilities survive a change in the responses being scored.

next.note: Study what happens when a policy optimizes this imperfect scorer.

study.title: The RLHF Book: Chapter 5, Reward Modeling
study.locator: The Default Reward Model Architecture; Implementation Example; Outcome Reward Models; Suggested Experiments, item 1, Train a Bradley-Terry reward model
study.depth: Use the preference experiment. Read outcome modeling to specify its label and pooling contract, not to add a process-reward implementation. The example's last-token index assumes right padding; do not copy it for left-padded inputs.

study.title: Reward-model training and evaluation implementation
study.locator: `build_preference_dataset`, `collate_fn`, `PreferenceRewardModel.get_reward`, `evaluate_preference_rm` and the accumulation loop in `train_preference_rm`
study.depth: Inspect rather than run the default full-backbone configuration. The final partial accumulation window uses a fixed divisor and is under-weighted; use accumulation 1 or correct the window weighting.

study.title: Length shifts in reward learning
study.locator: arXiv:2310.03716v2, Sections 3.1 and 4.2: length-stratified analysis and interventions on reward modeling

focus: Reuse the audited preference records, but split by prompt/conversation and near-duplicate group before expansion. Reserve distinct training, calibration and final evaluation prompts; freeze their manifests.
Use the last real token's hidden state under a declared EOS and padding convention. Count empty, invalid and token-identical truncated pairs instead of silently losing them.

Report pairwise accuracy, margins, probability NLL and Brier score. Fit any temperature only on calibration prompts and freeze it before final scoring. Report source/generator and response-length slices with counts.

A preference reward predicts relative choice under a rubric. An outcome head predicts a specified correctness label with its own token or sequence supervision; swapping these targets changes the meaning of calibration.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, reconstruct the path from two tokenized responses through their last real hidden states, one scalar head and stable pairwise loss. Add padding without changing the real tokens and require scores to agree within a declared dtype tolerance. Then repeat held-out scoring on a different generator or length slice without refitting either the reward head or its calibrator; record whether errors track correctness, length or style rather than assuming transfer.
traps: Using the last array position when it is padding, or using the count of real tokens as an index under left padding. Test both layouts or reject the unsupported one explicitly.
Reading the companion evaluator as a calibration audit. It reports pair-averaged loss, strict accuracy, mean rewards and mean margin; you must add calibration and shift slices.
Centering scores on each new policy's outputs. This changes the measurement scale and can conceal shift. Freeze calibration statistics and report raw scores too.

selfTest.q: Can ranking accuracy stay unchanged while probability NLL worsens?
selfTest.a: Yes. Enlarging correctly ordered but overconfident margins leaves order unchanged while increasing the cost of misranked or noisy comparisons. Evaluate probabilities, not only signs.

selfTest.q: A frozen backbone fits the training pairs. What has not been established?
selfTest.a: Held-out calibration, ranking under another policy, and behavior improvement after policy optimization. A reward-head fit alone establishes none of these.

selfTest.q: Why use a separate calibration split?
selfTest.a: Temperature or other calibration fitting is model selection. Using final evaluation labels for it leaks evaluation information into the scoring pipeline.

practice.name: RLHF Book Chapter 5 Suggested Experiments: Train a Bradley-Terry reward model
practice.locator: Suggested Experiments, item 1; adapt the linked preference reward-model implementation
practice.note: Freeze the backbone and train only the head on at most 1,000 audited training pairs with context at most 256 and batch 1. Use your immutable LMR-6 small-decoder SFT checkpoint, or its smaller CPU version, rather than the default model. Pin PyTorch 2.14.1 and, if using the companion loader, Transformers 5.19.0 and datasets 5.1.0. Keep separate calibration and held-out prompts; compare at least two fixed training seeds and save all attempts. The mini-project retains the shift, calibration and shortcut evidence.

units.stopWhen: Your head passes padding and identical-pair tests, and its frozen held-out report separates ranking, calibration and generator/length shift with counts and raw records, including a negative or inconclusive slice.

fit.note: Chapter 5 and its named experiment provide the real head-training path; the code and length-stratified study expose the padding, accumulation and shift contracts that the mini-project checks.

units.title: Reward overoptimization and the KL-regularized objective with a reference policy
outcomes: Derive the optimal policy of a fixed-reward, KL-regularized objective and state its support assumptions.
Distinguish a sampled log ratio, a policy KL estimate and an offline preference margin.
Explain why rising proxy reward can accompany worse independent behavior and why KL control is not a reward repair.
units.why: A reference policy constrains how a learned proxy is exploited. The derivation gives a precise optimization target, but it does not turn a misspecified reward into a trustworthy measure of behavior.

next.note: Substitute the optimal-policy expression into the preference likelihood.

study.title: DPO: the KL-regularized optimum
study.locator: arXiv:2305.18290v3, Section 3 equation 3; Section 4 equation 4; Appendix A.1, Deriving the Optimum of the KL-Constrained Reward Maximization Objective

study.title: The RLHF Book: Chapters 14 and 15, Over-Optimization and Regularization
study.locator: Chapter 14, Managing Proxy Objectives and Quantitative Over-Optimization; Chapter 15, KL Divergence in RL Optimization and Reference Model to Generations, at https://rlhfbook.com/c/15-regularization.html
study.depth: Use the KL definition from Entropy, cross-entropy, KL divergence and mutual information. Skip Chapter 15's implementation example here; derive the distribution and sampling units yourself. The book's claims that direct alignment fixes a KL distance are too strong: a fixed coefficient does not fix realized KL.

study.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
study.locator: arXiv:2210.10760v1, Sections 2 to 4, especially 2.1 Synthetic Data Setup, 3.5 RL vs BoN and 3.6 Effect of KL Penalty
study.depth: Read the proxy/gold design and its curve shapes, not a universal threshold. The gold scorer is a larger model standing in for humans, and the horizontal optimization measure uses the square root of KL.

focus: For each prompt and fixed reward, maximize \(J(\pi)=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}[r(x,y)]-\beta\operatorname{KL}(\pi\|\pi_{\text{ref}})\). Assume \(\beta>0\), finite normalizer and support compatible with the reference.

The solution is \(\pi^*(y\mid x)=\pi_{\text{ref}}(y\mid x)\exp(r(x,y)/\beta)/Z(x)\). Certify it by rewriting \(J(\pi)=\beta\log Z(x)-\beta\operatorname{KL}(\pi\|\pi^*)\), not only by taking derivatives.

A sampled sequence log ratio can be negative. Its expectation under the current policy gives the declared KL only with the correct sampling distribution, response support and termination convention. An average over fixed preference pairs is not that expectation.

Plot independent task quality beside proxy reward and policy drift. Different optimization procedures can exploit the same reward differently; the paper's best-of-many and RL results do not establish a universal safe KL budget.
units.reproduce: Derive the optimum closed-book. For one prompt with three possible completions, reference probabilities \((0.2,0.3,0.5)\), rewards \((\log 2,0,0)\) and \(\beta=1\), obtain \(Z=1.2\), optimal probabilities \((1/3,1/4,5/12)\) and objective \(\log 1.2\). Check normalization and the KL rewrite on CPU with PyTorch 2.14.1, `torch.float64`, natural logs and absolute tolerance \(10^{-12}\). No model or random sampling is involved.
traps: Treating a single negative sampled log ratio as a negative KL divergence. Non-negativity applies to the population divergence, not each draw.
Ignoring reference zeros. A policy putting mass where the reference is zero incurs infinite KL; finite offline observations do not certify useful coverage elsewhere.
Claiming a higher penalty guarantees safety. It restrains movement for a fixed reward optimization problem, but does not validate the reward or prescribe the realized drift of a finite training run.

selfTest.q: Why does a prompt-only reward offset not change the optimum?
selfTest.a: It multiplies every unnormalized probability for that prompt by the same factor, which cancels in normalization. The optimal objective value shifts, but the policy does not.

selfTest.q: Why is the gold score in Gao et al. not direct human evidence?
selfTest.a: A larger reward model supplies the synthetic labels and evaluation score. It permits controlled proxy/gold comparisons, but its errors and population coverage remain assumptions.

selfTest.q: What is wrong with calling the fixed preference-set mean log ratio the deployed policy KL?
selfTest.a: Its responses were not necessarily sampled from the current policy. Without the right sampling or weighting it measures a different distribution, even if the arithmetic is correct.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Score a KL-Regularized Policy Batch
practice.note: Free. Public cases cover positive sampled divergence, a mixed masked batch and a fully masked response. Keep its sum-over-response-tokens convention and do not clamp negative sampled divergences. These cases check supplied scores, not whether the responses came from the correct policy.

units.stopWhen: You certify the three-completion optimum, pass the named masked-batch examples, and can explain what additional independent evidence would expose reward overoptimization.

fit.note: The DPO appendix supplies the full derivation, the book and proxy/gold study cover exploitation limits, and the free masked-batch problem supplies checked practice.

units.title: The DPO derivation, \(\beta\), margins and gradient pressure
outcomes: Derive DPO by substituting the KL-optimal policy into a Bradley-Terry likelihood, retaining the partition term until it cancels.
Implement stable DPO from four response log-probability tensors and verify its policy-input gradients.
Explain how the adjusted margin, label noise and regularization coefficient affect update pressure without promising behavior gains.
units.why: The reparameterization removes a reward-model training stage, not the assumptions behind preference learning. The gradient reveals which mislabeled or poorly covered comparisons can dominate a bounded run.

next.note: Replace supplied scores with tested language-model response scores.

study.title: DPO: derivation and gradient
study.locator: arXiv:2305.18290v3, Section 4 equations 4 to 7 and What does the DPO update do?; Appendix A.2 and A.4, deriving the Bradley-Terry objective and its gradient

study.title: The RLHF Book: Chapter 8, Direct-Alignment Algorithms
study.locator: DPO Derivation: Deriving DPO Objectives for BT Models and Deriving the BT DPO Gradient; Implementation Details
study.depth: Use the derivation and loss listing, not the claim that KL is static or that each update reaches the optimal policy. Finite-data, finite-step fitting need not recover the population optimum.

study.title: Stable differential reference for the pair loss
study.locator: `DPOLoss.forward`: chosen/rejected log ratios, stable logistic loss and detached logging metrics
study.depth: Use the executable two-term smoothing expression if exploring soft labels. Ignore the nearby comment that combines a sum of log sigmoids into the log of their sum; that algebra is invalid.

focus: Let \(\ell_\theta(y)=\log\pi_\theta(y\mid x)\), \(\ell_{\text{ref}}(y)=\log\pi_{\text{ref}}(y\mid x)\), and \(m=[\ell_\theta(y_w)-\ell_\theta(y_l)]-[\ell_{\text{ref}}(y_w)-\ell_{\text{ref}}(y_l)]\). The pair loss is \(L=-\log\sigma(\beta m)\).

Recover \(r(x,y)=\beta\log[\pi^*(y\mid x)/\pi_{\text{ref}}(y\mid x)]+\beta\log Z(x)\). Only a shared prompt lets the partition term cancel in the pair likelihood. State the fixed-reference, Bradley-Terry and support assumptions.

The scalar derivative is \(\partial L/\partial m=-\beta\sigma(-\beta m)\). Its magnitude is greater for negative than positive margins at the same coefficient. A mislabeled hard pair can therefore exert substantial pressure.

The reference is frozen. The coefficient controls both loss scaling and the population reward/KL trade-off; changing it is not merely changing the learning rate, nor a guarantee of monotonic realized KL.
units.reproduce: Derive the substitution and margin gradient without notes. On CPU with PyTorch 2.14.1 and `torch.float64`, use policy chosen/rejected log probabilities -3 and -5, reference chosen/rejected -4 and -5, and \(\beta=0.4\). Obtain \(m=1\), loss 0.5130152523999526, and policy-input derivatives approximately -0.1605249359550192 and 0.1605249359550192. Match the pinned `DPOLoss` and `torch.autograd.gradcheck`; compare these values with absolute tolerance \(10^{-12}\). Repeat stable loss evaluation at scaled logits -1000 and 1000, requiring finite losses and gradients rather than nonzero gradients at saturation.
traps: Subtracting the reference gap in the wrong direction. Write all four scores before simplifying the margin.
Using detached implicit rewards to form the training loss. Detachment is for reporting only; the policy scores in the loss must retain their graph.

Saying every parameter update raises the chosen probability and lowers the rejected probability. The scalar score derivatives have opposite signs, but shared model parameters and probability normalization can move both probabilities down.

selfTest.q: At identical policy and reference scores, is there no learning signal?
selfTest.a: The adjusted margin is zero and loss is \(\log 2\), but the margin derivative is \(-\beta/2\). The parameter gradient need not vanish unless the two policy-score gradients cancel.

selfTest.q: Does increasing the coefficient always increase gradient magnitude?
selfTest.a: No. At a fixed positive margin, the coefficient multiplies a sigmoid weight that decreases as the scaled margin grows. At zero margin the magnitude is \(\beta/2\); negative margins behave differently.

selfTest.q: Does the derivation prove that an offline DPO run equals online RLHF in behavior?
selfTest.a: No. It reparameterizes a preference model through the optimal policy of a specified KL-regularized reward problem. Coverage, model fit, optimization and preference-model assumptions still limit the learned policy.

practice.name: TensorTonic: Implement the DPO Loss
practice.locator: Implement `direct_preference_optimization_loss(policy_chosen, policy_rejected, reference_chosen, reference_rejected, beta, label_smoothing)`
practice.note: Free. Public cases cover a positive margin, mixed margin signs and a zero margin with smoothing; strict reward ties count as incorrect. They do not test gradients or text masking. Add the independent derivative check above before using a model.

units.stopWhen: You derive the complete substitution, pass the public score examples and match the independent gradient oracle, including finite extreme-logit behavior.

fit.note: The original derivation and book gradient reach derive depth; pinned executable loss code and the free score problem support independent numerical and gradient checks.

units.title: Response-only log probabilities, masks and reference-checkpoint identity
outcomes: Compute shifted response-only log probabilities with explicit prompt, padding, EOS and truncation rules.
Bind reference scores to the exact checkpoint, tokenizer, template and scored token sequence.
Demonstrate that reference mismatch changes policy gradients even when the policy scores stay fixed.
units.why: The four scalars in a DPO loss are meaningful only if they score the same conditional events. A stale reference cache or a shifted completion mask silently defines a different experiment.

next.note: Turn boundary and identity failures into preflight regressions.

study.title: Shifted sequence-scoring reference
study.locator: `compute_logprobs`: the logit, label and mask shifts; gathered token scores; `average_log_prob` branches
study.depth: Pass a completion-and-padding mask, not merely the attention mask suggested by the helper's docstring. Its average branch is a different score convention, not ordinary summed DPO.

study.title: CS336 Spring 2026 Assignment 5 supplement: model-to-loss contract
study.locator: Section 6.3, Implementing the DPO Loss, Problem `dpo_loss`, printed p. 17: Alpaca template, appended EOS and `run_compute_per_instance_dpo_loss`
study.depth: Use the public tiny-model test on CPU. Skip Section 6.4's two-device training recipe; the bounded comparison uses your own SFT checkpoint. Prompt cancellation requires the exact same tokenized prefix in both branches, not merely similar prompt text.

study.title: TRL 1.15.0: preprocessing and frozen-reference configuration
study.locator: Expected dataset type and format; Preprocessing and tokenization; DPOTrainer `ref_model`; DPOConfig `precompute_ref_log_probs`, `sync_ref_model`, `disable_dropout` and loss types

focus: Score each response token from its preceding context. Shift the labels and completion mask together with the causal prediction boundary. Prompt tokens condition the model but do not enter the response sum.
Keep attention and loss masks distinct. Include EOS under one declared rule, exclude padding, and reject or separately count pairs whose distinguishing response is lost to truncation.

Hash the frozen reference weights and adapter state, tokenizer revision, template, exact token IDs, masks, EOS/truncation rules and score convention into cache identity. A filename or model family is not sufficient.

TRL 1.15.0 defaults to `loss_type=["sigmoid"]`, `beta=0.1` and summed completion scores. `sigmoid_norm` changes the aggregation. The trainer rejects a policy and reference that are the same object; keep reference synchronization off for this fixed-reference study.
units.reproduce: On CPU with PyTorch 2.14.1 and `torch.float64`, use zero logits of shape `(1, 5, 3)`, token IDs `[[0, 1, 2, 0, 1]]` and unshifted completion mask `[[0, 0, 1, 1, 0]]`. Derive score \(-2\log 3\); only logit positions 1 and 2 receive score gradients. Match `compute_logprobs` within absolute tolerance \(10^{-12}\). Then hold the preceding unit's policy scores and coefficient fixed, changing only the reference chosen score from -4 to -2. Loss becomes 0.9130152523999526 and the chosen policy-input derivative becomes approximately -0.2394750640449808. The rejection score stays -5. Confirm the altered gradient and require the manifest to reject that cache mismatch.
traps: Tokenizing prompt and response independently without inspecting the join. Boundary tokenization can differ from tokenizing the formatted sequence; inspect actual IDs and the first scored token.
Assuming equal initial policy/reference values imply zero parameter gradient. The reference must be fixed independently, not connected to the policy's autograd graph.
Equating a mean token log probability with a sequence log probability. Changing sum to mean changes pair weighting and the objective, especially with unequal response lengths.

selfTest.q: Which state changes invalidate a precomputed reference score?
selfTest.a: Anything changing the reference conditional event or its probability: weights/adapters, tokenizer, template, token IDs, masking, EOS, truncation or aggregation. Recompute rather than mixing identities.

selfTest.q: Does this one-pair reference mismatch reverse the chosen-score derivative?
selfTest.a: No. With a positive coefficient its sign stays negative. The changed reference margin changes the gradient's weight; across shared model parameters and many pairs that can change the update direction.

selfTest.q: How should you check a cached reference on a model batch?
selfTest.a: Reload the exact frozen checkpoint in deterministic evaluation mode and rescore the same IDs and masks. Compare within a dtype-specific tolerance and verify the full manifest before accepting the cache.

practice.name: CS336 Assignment 5 supplement: `dpo_loss`
practice.locator: Section 6.3; connect `run_compute_per_instance_dpo_loss` and run `uv run pytest -k test_per_instance_dpo_loss`
practice.note: The public test uses tiny policy/reference fixtures and a local word tokenizer, then compares one scalar loss to its expected value. It does not check gradients or every mask boundary. Add unequal response lengths, padding, prompt-boundary and stale-reference tests yourself. Use PyTorch 2.14.1 and Transformers 5.19.0 for your recorded implementation, and keep solutions private.

units.stopWhen: Your scorer passes the public tiny-model scalar check and your independent mask and reference-mismatch gradient tests, while cached scores are accepted only under matching manifests.

fit.note: The scoring helper, located assignment and versioned TRL contract cover response boundaries and reference identity; independent gradients cover what the public scalar test does not.

units.title: Preference-data audits and objective sign, gradient and invariance tests
outcomes: Build an audit ledger for provenance, duplicate groups, split leakage, raw votes and presentation/length slices.
Test objective signs, gradients, numerical stability and valid invariances against an independent oracle.
Inject reversed labels, reference mismatch and mask/normalization errors and retain a failing regression for each.
units.why: A healthy training curve cannot distinguish a correct objective from a consistently reversed label pipeline. Preflight tests must catch failures before the preference route spends its training budget.

next.note: Only audited data and a checked objective enter the behavior comparison.

study.title: CS336: pair inspection and the checked model-to-loss path
study.locator: Sections 6.2 and 6.3, Problems `look_at_hh` and `dpo_loss`; revisit the raw records and the public scalar test, not the full training run

study.title: The RLHF Book: audit-sensitive collection and optimization
study.locator: Chapter 11, Collecting Preference Data, Multiturn Data and Bias: Things to Watch Out For in Data Collection; Chapter 8, Implementation Details and Suggested Experiments item 4, Change the data before changing the loss, at https://rlhfbook.com/c/08-direct-alignment.html

study.title: TRL 1.15.0: logs and objective conventions
study.locator: Computing the loss, Loss Types and Logged metrics; DPOConfig `loss_type`, `label_smoothing` and `beta`
study.depth: Use the default sigmoid branch as a differential reference, not the catalog as an assignment. Keep the explicit response-score oracle independent of trainer preprocessing.

focus: Audit both raw and model-visible data: prompt/candidate duplicates, source licenses and provenance, prompt-group leakage, label polarity, ties, annotator agreement, length/style balance, truncation and post-tokenization identical pairs. Save counts and reasons at every filter.
Compare scratch loss and policy-input gradients against analytic values before comparing to library code. Then check an actual batch with the frozen reference and the same IDs and completion masks.

Batch permutation and whole-batch duplication preserve a mean loss. Common chosen/rejected score offsets cancel within each model. These invariances do not justify changing one response, reference gap or length convention.

Seed corrupted copies, never overwrite the clean manifest: swapped labels, duplicate leakage, non-response mask bits, sum-to-mean replacement and stale reference scores. Require the intended check to fail and then pass after repair.
units.reproduce: Assemble a CPU preflight suite with PyTorch 2.14.1 and `torch.float64` from the previous units' loss, derivative, mask and reference-mismatch oracles. On the fixed pair with scaled margin \(z=0.4\), swap chosen and rejected in both policy and reference scores. Verify \(L(-z)-L(z)=z\) within absolute tolerance \(10^{-12}\), and verify that gradients now pressure the opposite response identity. Also test identical tokenized responses through the same deterministic scorer: loss is \(\log 2\) and the shared model-parameter gradient is zero. Preserve the failures from a single-sided swap and a stale cache as separate diagnoses.
traps: Calling label reversal an invariance of the loss. Swapping the two outcomes negates the logit; the loss generally changes. Batch permutation is an invariance, label polarity is not.

Requiring zero gradients for independent equal-valued chosen/rejected score tensors. Their partial derivatives are opposite and nonzero; cancellation occurs through the shared model graph for identical responses.
Claiming prompt decontamination from an exact-string check alone. State the normalization and duplicate-group rule, review matches and bound the claim; paraphrases may remain.

selfTest.q: Why can initial loss fail to expose reversed labels?
selfTest.a: With matching policy and reference, both label orientations have zero adjusted margin and loss \(\log 2\). Check the response-identity gradient and the raw label provenance, not only the loss.

selfTest.q: Which gradient should whole-batch duplication preserve?
selfTest.a: For the same deterministic model and a mean reduction, the aggregated model-parameter gradient. Independent per-copy input-score gradients can each be smaller because there are more averaged entries.

selfTest.q: Can the public DPO test certify this entire preflight?
selfTest.a: No. It checks one scalar fixture. Data lineage, leakage, response boundaries, gradients and reference-cache identity require independent tests.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: the versioned preference audit and preflight failure campaign, including annotator-noise, swapped-label, mask, normalization and reference-mismatch regressions.
units.stopWhen: Your clean manifest passes preflight, every seeded defect fails a named independent check, and the retained report distinguishes data failure from loss or reference failure.

fit.note: The located data and loss paths plus versioned trainer conventions cover the tested contracts; the mini-project supplies the integrated audit and seeded failure campaign.

units.title: External evaluation and the versioned sampling, labeling and optimization loop
outcomes: Compare untouched SFT, chosen-only SFT and DPO under matched or explicitly disclosed training and generation budgets.
Evaluate capability, safety, calibration and diversity on held-out prompts never used for preference training or selection.
Version a sampling, labeling, optimization and rollback loop while retaining failed runs and inconclusive results.
units.why: Preference accuracy is an internal diagnostic. The section's result is a bounded claim about a language model's external behavior, supported by controls that separate training from longer answers, sampling changes and judge preferences.

next.note: Optional: compare mechanisms without turning the study into an objective sweep.
Carry the frozen baselines and evaluator forward to the RL route.

study.title: DPO: evaluation contracts and judge validation
study.locator: arXiv:2305.18290v3, Section 6, Tasks, Evaluation and Methods; Sections 6.3, Generalization to a new input distribution, and 6.4, Validating GPT-4 judgments with human judgments
study.depth: Read the controls and evaluator comparison. Paid judge calls and the paper's model sizes are not required; use your frozen local task scorer and blinded manual review.

study.title: Tulu 3: preference-data and recipe ablations
study.locator: arXiv:2411.15124v5, Sections 5.2 to 5.4: From Prompts to Preference Data, Key Findings of Data Ablations, and Preference Tuning Recipe and Analyses; Figure 7 and Table 18
study.depth: Trace one data-source ablation and one objective comparison. Do not reproduce the model pool, proprietary annotation or distributed training. Its final recipe uses length-normalized DPO, not the original summed loss.

study.title: CS336 supplement: after-training behavior checks
study.locator: Section 6.4, Problem `dpo_training`, parts (b) to (d): preference, safety and capability comparison
study.depth: Replace hosted judging with manual review and small local capability/safety subsets. In 6.4's preceding paragraph, raw chosen likelihood exceeding rejected likelihood is not implicit reward accuracy: use the reference-adjusted margin instead.

focus: Freeze the LMR-5 evaluator, prompt groups, parser, decoding, output budget, tie/failure policy and selection rule before training. Final prompts and labels must not enter preference collection, calibration or checkpoint selection.

Keep an untouched SFT control and a chosen-only SFT control trained on the same audited data. Match update-token or compute budgets where possible; disclose reference-scoring, labeling, candidate generation and any mismatch rather than calling equal steps equal compute.

Report independent task correctness, harmful compliance and benign refusal separately, probability calibration on a defined labeled task, and diversity/repetition at matched sampling settings. Every preference win rate includes both response-length distributions, item counts, tie handling and prompt-group uncertainty.

Use development-only interventions for label noise, \(\beta\), data size, length/style controls and judge swaps. Archive failed/inconclusive runs, then freeze one candidate for untouched final evaluation and a clean-state repeat. A changed judge or rubric starts a new version of the loop.
units.reproduce: Rebuild a report from a fixed synthetic six-prompt ledger, not its summary: candidate outcomes are three wins, two losses and one tie; candidate token lengths are `[20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70]` and baseline lengths are `[30, 30, 30, 30, 30, 30]`. With ties counted as half-wins and all six prompts retained, obtain win rate \(7/12\), candidate mean length 45 and baseline mean length 30. The token counts use one declared tokenizer; this arithmetic fixture is not model evidence. Explain why the result alone cannot establish a length-independent gain, then use the same raw-record accounting on your bounded study.
traps: Selecting a checkpoint or a rubric on the final held-out scores. That set becomes development data; reserve a new untouched set for the final claim.
Dropping invalid generations or failed attempts from the denominator. Keep them under the predeclared scoring rule and report their counts.
Calling a small positive win-rate difference a gain without uncertainty or length/style controls. A failed control or broad interval supports a narrower or inconclusive claim.

selfTest.q: Preference accuracy rose while held-out task accuracy fell. Which result decides the claim?
selfTest.a: The external outcome and predeclared gates. Rising preference accuracy cannot override a capability or safety regression; preserve the negative result and diagnose the mechanism.

selfTest.q: Why keep chosen-only SFT when you already have untouched SFT?
selfTest.a: It tests whether gains come from extra exposure to the preferred responses rather than the contrastive objective. Account for its different token and reference-scoring cost.

selfTest.q: What must be versioned to roll back a labeling round?
selfTest.a: The generating and reference checkpoints, sampling config, prompt split, raw outputs/votes, rubric or judge, filters, training settings, evaluator and selected artifact. Roll back to a complete accepted manifest, not just a weight file.

practice.name: RLHF Book Chapter 8 Suggested Experiments: small DPO run and data intervention
practice.locator: Suggested Experiments items 1 and 4: Train a small DPO run on UltraFeedback; Change the data before changing the loss
practice.note: Adapt to your audited preference subset and immutable LMR-6 small-decoder SFT checkpoint: at most 1,000 pairs, context at most 256, batch 1 and at most 100 updates per trained arm. Use your GPU or the smaller CPU decoder, with precomputed frozen reference scores if needed. Pin PyTorch 2.14.1; for a TRL implementation also pin TRL 1.15.0, Transformers 5.19.0 and datasets 5.1.0. Compare at least two fixed seeds, keep the objective unchanged for the noise intervention, and state the reduced-scale limits. The section mini-project retains the baselines, held-out behavior, length/style/judge controls and rollback record.

units.stopWhen: A clean-state repeat reconstructs your selected comparison from manifests and raw held-out outputs, and your report states whether the gain survives length, style, judge and failure controls or remains inconclusive.

fit.note: The original evaluation design, Tulu data/recipe ablations and supplement behavior checks cover the research loop; the named small-run experiment feeds the mini-project's external comparison.

units.title: IPO, SimPO and ORPO, and constitution-conditioned AI feedback
outcomes: Contrast IPO, SimPO and ORPO by feedback contract, score normalization, reference dependence and optimization pressure.
Separate constitution-conditioned comparison labeling from critique/revision instruction tuning.
Specify one optional mechanism-isolating comparison without reusing its training judge as the final evaluator.
units.why: This optional unit gives enough mechanism vocabulary to evaluate a proposed alternative, not a catalog to train. An objective change and an AI-labeling change are separate interventions and need separate controls.

next.note: Connect constitutional feedback to safety-data lineage and revision.
Optional broader study of preference and policy-optimization families.

study.title: IPO: a finite squared-margin target
study.locator: arXiv:2310.12036v2, Section 4.2, Weak Regularisation and Overfitting; Section 5.2, Sampled Loss for IPO, equation 17 and Algorithm 1
study.depth: Read the failure case and sampled loss. Skip the full general-framework proof. The book's Chapter 8 variant bullet incorrectly associates IPO with a logit transform: IPO uses the identity transform; use this paper for the distinction.

study.title: SimPO: normalized policy score without a reference
study.locator: arXiv:2405.14734v3, Sections 2.2 and 2.3, equations 3 to 6: length-normalized reward and target reward margin
study.depth: Stop after the objective and the discussion of drift without KL regularization. Length normalization does not by itself validate behavior or remove all length effects.

study.title: ORPO: preference pressure inside an SFT objective
study.locator: arXiv:2403.07691v2, Sections 3 and 4, especially 4.1 Preliminaries and 4.2 Objective Function of ORPO
study.depth: Stop before the training configurations. Note that its odds use the paper's length-normalized probability score, not the raw product of token probabilities.

study.title: Constitutional AI: which principle generated the label?
study.locator: arXiv:2212.08073v1, Figure 1; Sections 3.1 and 4.1, Method; Appendix C.2, Principles for RL-CAI
study.depth: Trace the data transformations and one comparison principle, not the large-model training. Human helpfulness labels remain in the paper's mixed preference model; AI harmlessness labels do not mean human values disappeared.

focus: IPO's sampled objective regresses the reference-adjusted log-ratio margin toward \((2\tau)^{-1}\); its \(\tau\) occupies DPO's \(\beta\) regularization role. A squared finite target differs from logistic pressure that keeps rewarding larger margins on deterministic labels.

SimPO uses \(\beta\log\pi_\theta(y\mid x)/|y|\) as a reward and subtracts a target margin inside the logistic argument. It removes the reference and changes normalization and margin together; a comparison must isolate these changes rather than attribute everything to reference removal.

ORPO combines chosen-response SFT loss with a weighted negative log-sigmoid of a chosen/rejected log-odds ratio. No reference model is required, but the SFT component and odds transformation must remain explicit in the contract.

A constitution conditions label generation through the feedback model's interpretation of a principle. Store the exact principle, judge revision, order, prompt and output with each comparison; keep an external human-checked or executable anchor for correlated judge/policy errors.
units.reproduce: Without notes, make a four-row contract table for DPO, IPO, SimPO and ORPO: feedback unit, score aggregation, reference, margin or target, and chosen-only term. Trace one Appendix C.2 constitutional principle through Section 4.1's comparison-label path, then contrast it with Section 3.1's critique/revision-to-SFT path. Mark what would change in your manifests and controls if only the labeling principle changed. No additional model training is needed for this explanation check.
traps: Treating TRL's `sigmoid_norm` as full SimPO. It changes length aggregation but retains reference-adjusted scores; SimPO also removes the reference and adds a margin.
Comparing raw losses across objective families. Squared margins, logistic losses and SFT mixtures have different scales and optima; compare matched external behavior instead.
Interpreting a principle as a proof of label correctness. The feedback model can misunderstand it, prefer its own style or follow a presentation artifact.

selfTest.q: What distinguishes IPO from simply stopping DPO earlier?
selfTest.a: IPO changes the sampled loss to a squared target-margin fit. Early stopping changes the optimization trajectory of the logistic objective; it does not make the objectives identical.

selfTest.q: Does removing the reference make an objective identical to chosen-only SFT?
selfTest.a: No. SimPO and ORPO still compare chosen and rejected responses. Chosen-only SFT uses no rejected-response contrast.

selfTest.q: Does constitution-conditioned AI feedback require DPO?
selfTest.a: No. It is a labeling method. The original paper distills AI comparisons into a preference model and uses RL, while critique/revision examples support a separate supervised stage.

units.practiceNote: The section mini-project covers this: the optional objective-contract comparison and a principle-conditioned label-provenance audit, without requiring a second full training sweep or a paid judge.
units.stopWhen: You can explain the four contracts and the two constitutional data paths, and propose one controlled optional change with its independent evaluation and lineage consequences.

fit.note: The pool covers objective variants and general AI-labeler prompting, but lacks the explicit constitutional critique/revision versus comparison pipeline. The opened Constitutional AI paper fills that coverage gap with Sections 3.1, 4.1 and Appendix C.2.
